claims.statement: A published model of the human colonic crypt adopts a mean cell radius of 5 micrometres, giving a working cell diameter of about 10 micrometres.
claims.scope: A working diameter for one crypt cell, used only to convert a migration speed into a fraction of a cell position per hour.
claims.uncertainty: It is a model parameter rather than a measurement of a specific cell, and cell size varies with position in the crypt and with differentiation state. The doubling of the radius to a diameter is arithmetic, not a separate finding.

claims.statement: WNT signalling decreases progressively up the colonic crypt axis; the stem cells at the crypt base are characterised by high WNT activity; and colon cells receive WNT signals from the surrounding mesenchyme or stroma, with mesenchymal cells near the crypt base secreting WNT ligands while those positioned distally do not.
claims.scope: The direction of the Wnt activity gradient along the crypt axis and the location of the cells that secrete the ligands, in the healthy adult human colon.
claims.uncertainty: The review states the direction of the gradient and the location of its source, not the shape of the concentration profile, its absolute values, or the mechanism by which it is established. The lesson keeps those three questions separate and treats the mechanism as unsettled in its own scene.

claims.statement: Cells of the colonic crypt differentiate as they migrate upward and are fully differentiated at the crypt top.
claims.scope: The direction of differentiation along the crypt axis in the healthy adult human colon.
claims.uncertainty: The source describes the direction of differentiation without assigning states to numbered cell positions. The lesson's cell at 'roughly the seventeenth position' is an illustration and is flagged as such in the scene.

claims.statement: Cells in the lower half of the human colonic crypt migrate upward at an average speed of around 4 micrometres per hour.
claims.scope: The measured average upward migration speed in the lower half of a normal human colonic crypt, used to show that a cell moves while it averages a concentration.
claims.uncertainty: The figure is reported for the lower half of the crypt only, where most of the study's sections were collected, and the lesson does not extend it over the whole climb. The comparison with a 10-micrometre cell diameter is the lesson's own arithmetic and is presented as an estimate.

claims.statement: An extracellular signal molecule that binds a receptor is a ligand, and cell-surface receptor proteins act as signal transducers: they convert an extracellular ligand-binding event into intracellular signals that alter the behaviour of the target cell.
claims.scope: The general definitions of ligand and of signal transduction by cell-surface receptors, as used to frame the four parts of a signalling system.
claims.uncertainty: The source is a 2002 textbook edition. These are stable general definitions rather than time-sensitive findings, and nothing quantitative is taken from it here. The four-part plus termination framing is the lesson's own organisation of the material.

claims.statement: Wnt signalling is driven by the activity of a receptor complex of Frizzled and LRP5/6 when bound by Wnt ligands.
claims.scope: The identity of the receptor for canonical Wnt signalling in the colonic crypt.
claims.uncertainty: The lesson's statement that one Wnt molecule occupies one receptor complex, so that reception multiplies nothing, is the lesson's reading of what a binding event is rather than a stoichiometric measurement quoted from the source.

claims.statement: In the absence of Wnt ligands a destruction complex forms that includes APC, Axin, CK1A and GSK3B; phosphorylation of beta-catenin by CK1A and GSK3B marks it for ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal degradation, so little beta-catenin accumulates.
claims.scope: The composition and action of the beta-catenin destruction complex in the unstimulated state.
claims.uncertainty: The review also lists Dishevelled among the complex's components. This lesson names only the four above and says the complex 'includes' them, because Dishevelled's placement is described differently across the literature; nothing taught here depends on settling that. The lesson does not claim the four named components are the complete membership.

claims.statement: When Wnt binds its receptor complex, the destruction complex is recruited to the cell membrane, which leads to an increase in available beta-catenin; the signal therefore raises beta-catenin by interfering with its degradation rather than by increasing its synthesis.
claims.scope: The immediate consequence of Wnt binding for the destruction complex and for the amount of available beta-catenin.
claims.uncertainty: The source states the recruitment and the resulting increase. The lesson's added gloss, that synthesis was never the limiting step and destruction was, is an interpretation of that mechanism rather than a separately sourced measurement of synthesis and degradation rates.

claims.statement: On exposure to a localised Wnt cue, the endogenous beta-catenin destruction complex in human colon epithelial cells reorients towards the cue while maintaining its composition and its binding to beta-catenin and moving towards the plasma membrane; the study's authors propose from this that the complex relocates rather than disassembling.
claims.scope: What happens to the destruction complex on Wnt exposure in cultured human colon epithelial cells, including a non-transformed line as well as colorectal cancer lines.
claims.uncertainty: Relocation rather than disassembly is the authors' proposal from immunofluorescence localisation and pull-down data in cultured cells, and the lesson reports it as their proposal. Cultured lines, several cancer-derived, are not a crypt in a living colon. Relocation is also only part of the story: a separate review finds residual activity after stimulation coming mainly from complexes that did not move, so this claim is not offered as a complete account of how destruction slows.

claims.statement: Beta-catenin that escapes degradation acts with the transcription factors TCF and LEF, and the genes switched on include c-MYC, LGR5 and cyclin D1.
claims.scope: The transcriptional output of canonical Wnt signalling in the colonic crypt, at the level of three named target genes.
claims.uncertainty: The review names further targets including c-JUN, OCT4 and SOX2, which the lesson does not list. The characterisation of these genes as 'the programme of a dividing, undifferentiated cell' is the lesson's summary; the source names the targets rather than supplying that gloss.

claims.statement: What happens when a signal is withdrawn matters as much as what happens when it arrives, and the effect of a signal is transitory because the signal acts by altering a set of molecules that are themselves unstable and undergoing continual turnover.
claims.scope: The general principle of signal termination through the turnover of the molecules a signal alters.
claims.uncertainty: The lesson's application of the principle to Wnt, that the destruction complex runs continuously so termination requires nothing new to be made, follows from that principle together with the separately sourced constitutive action of the complex. It is the lesson's synthesis rather than a statement quoted about Wnt.

claims.statement: A single gene reading a single threshold on a morphogen gradient with a monotonous response function carries at most one bit of positional information, distinguishing only two regions; the mapping between position and local cue values can be noisy or ambiguous, and cells exceed this ceiling by using gene-to-gene interactions and spatial coupling rather than independent thresholds alone.
claims.scope: The information-theoretic ceiling on threshold reading of a monotonic gradient, and the general finding that real systems exceed it by other means.
claims.uncertainty: The ceiling is a result about an idealised reading arrangement, not a measurement of any tissue. The lesson's own arithmetic extends it: that 32 zones would need 31 nested thresholds, and that those 31 thresholds carry only about 5 bits between them rather than 31, because thresholds on one monotonic gradient are nested and therefore redundant. That reconciliation of 5 with 31 is the lesson's reasoning from the source's one-bit ceiling, and it assumes independent genes, one threshold each, a monotonic gradient and no noise. No equivalent measurement is available for the human colonic crypt.

claims.statement: The four primary gap genes of the Drosophila embryo were estimated to carry 4.2 plus or minus 0.05 bits of positional information, sufficient for each nucleus to determine its location to roughly 1 per cent relative precision.
claims.scope: A quantitative estimate of positional information carried by a four-gene readout in the early fruit-fly embryo, used as the best-characterised case of how much position a gradient system can supply.
claims.uncertainty: It is an estimate for an insect embryo, which is a syncytium of nuclei in shared cytoplasm rather than a sheet of separate cells, and it is quoted as an estimate rather than a direct measurement. The lesson states explicitly that it is not the crypt's value and that no equivalent figure is offered for the human colonic crypt. The comparison of 4.2 bits against the 4 bits four independent binary switches could carry, and against the roughly 2.3 bits four single-threshold genes on one gradient would give, is the lesson's own arithmetic.

claims.statement: Because molecules arrive at random, the width of the region a system can localise itself to from a concentration gradient shrinks in proportion to the averaging time raised to the power minus one half, so halving the positional uncertainty costs four times the averaging time.
claims.scope: The scaling of positional precision with averaging time and copy number, in theoretical models of gradients used for positioning inside a single cell.
claims.uncertainty: The source models subcellular positioning of the kind bacteria use to find their own middle, not a tissue-scale gradient across an epithelium. What the lesson transfers is the structure of the argument and the inverse-square-root scaling, both consequences of molecules arriving at random. The lesson deliberately quotes no molecule or receptor count from this source, because it found no published figure for the number of Wnt receptors on a human colonic crypt cell and did not want to imply one by analogy. The four-times-for-half consequence is the lesson's arithmetic on the scaling law.

claims.statement: A relay chain is called a signalling cascade when it contains multiple amplification steps, so whether a given pathway amplifies is a question about that pathway rather than something settled by the label.
claims.scope: The textbook definition of a signalling cascade, used to make amplification an empirical question in this lesson.
claims.uncertainty: The definition is the source's; the inference that applying the word to every pathway and reading amplification back out of it is circular is the lesson's own argument. Usage of 'cascade' in the wider literature is looser than this definition.

claims.statement: In visual transduction a single activated rhodopsin molecule catalyses the activation of hundreds of transducin molecules at about 1000 per second, each activated transducin activates one cyclic GMP phosphodiesterase, each phosphodiesterase hydrolyses about 4000 cyclic GMP molecules per second, and the chain hydrolyses more than 10 to the fifth cyclic GMP molecules for a single quantum of light absorbed.
claims.scope: The amplification figures of the vertebrate phototransduction cascade, used as this lesson's contrasting case of a genuinely high-gain pathway.
claims.uncertainty: Textbook values from a 2002 edition, and orders of magnitude rather than precise constants. The final figure is a count of molecules hydrolysed per single absorbed quantum, a per-event catalytic tally, which the lesson distinguishes explicitly from the dimensionless steady-state ratio quoted for the Wnt pathway; the two are not compared numerically. Identifying which two of the three steps multiply is the lesson's own reading of the quoted numbers.

claims.statement: In a quantitative model of the canonical Wnt pathway built on measurements in Xenopus egg extracts, moving from the reference state to the standard stimulated state raises the concentration of free non-phosphorylated beta-catenin by a factor of approximately 6, from 25 to 153 nanomolar.
claims.scope: The magnitude of the beta-catenin response to Wnt stimulation in the best-characterised quantitative account of the canonical pathway, used to test whether this pathway amplifies strongly.
claims.uncertainty: The values come from a fitted model of a frog egg extract system, not a measurement inside a human colonic crypt cell, and the lesson says so. A model's stimulated state is a chosen reference condition. Critically, this figure is a dimensionless ratio of two steady-state concentrations and is NOT commensurable with the phototransduction figure, which counts molecules hydrolysed per absorbed photon. The lesson states that the two cannot be divided into one another and makes no claim about how many orders of magnitude separate the two pathways' gains. No per-event catalytic tally for the Wnt pathway was found in any source consulted.

claims.statement: Across genetic and pharmacological perturbations in a human colorectal cancer line, the absolute level of beta-catenin after Wnt stimulation spanned roughly 30 to 1200 nanomolar while the fold change stayed around 6 to 9; the study's authors propose that the fold change, rather than the final absolute level, is what the downstream transcriptional system reads, which would require a cell to compare its beta-catenin level after the signal with the level before it.
claims.scope: The relative constancy of fold change against the variability of absolute level in one human cell line, and the authors' proposal about what the pathway's output is.
claims.uncertainty: The authors present this as evidence for a hypothesis and note it challenges previous understanding; the lesson carries it at that confidence. Measurements are in a colorectal cancer line, not normal crypt tissue. The lesson uses it in two further places as a possibility to hold open rather than an established account: to qualify the claim that the cell reads only the level here and now, and to show that the APC conclusion in the final scene holds under either reading. It also distinguishes the short-term baseline this hypothesis would need from a record of distance travelled, which scene 1 rules out and which this hypothesis does not restore.

claims.statement: Wnt proteins are hydrophobic because of a lipid modification, which creates the problem of explaining how they travel through aqueous extracellular space; palmitoylation is essential for Wnt secretion, and mutation of the conserved serine residue or loss of Porcupine activity leaves Wnt retained in the endoplasmic reticulum.
claims.scope: The chemical property of Wnt proteins that makes their spread difficult to explain, and the requirement for lipid modification in secretion.
claims.uncertainty: The review states the requirement for palmitoylation and the consequence of losing it. The lesson does not describe the chemistry of the modification, which belongs to lipid and protein chemistry outcomes elsewhere in the course.

claims.statement: Whether Wnts act as long-range signalling molecules has been a long-debated question and the exact range of their action is not known; lipoproteins, heparan sulphate proteoglycans, exosomes and cytonemes have each been proposed as transport routes, with some mechanisms operating simultaneously and others context-dependent, and the proposal that Wnts travel as oligomers or micelles is contradicted by the finding in flies that blocking the movement of one labelled form of Wingless did not affect the spreading of a differently labelled form.
claims.scope: The unsettled state of the mechanism by which Wnt ligands spread from their source, and the specific proposals under consideration.
claims.uncertainty: This claim records that the field is unsettled, which is what the review states; it is not a claim that any one mechanism is correct. The review's own hedging language includes remains unclear, poorly understood, controversial, and proposed mechanism, and the lesson carries the uncertainty at that level. Much of the underlying work is in Drosophila rather than human colon.

claims.statement: Analysis of Wnt3 in mouse intestinal crypts showed a short-range distribution mediated via lateral transcytosis, meaning the ligand is passed between neighbouring cells rather than released to diffuse freely through the extracellular space.
claims.scope: The reported mode of Wnt3 spread in mouse intestinal crypts, presented as one of the competing readings of how a crypt gradient is formed.
claims.uncertainty: The lesson reads this in a 2021 review that reports a 2016 primary study; the primary study was not itself retrieved, and the lesson attributes the finding to work reported in the review rather than presenting it as first-hand. The work is in mouse small intestine and concerns Wnt3, whereas this block follows the human colonic crypt, where the review identifies the mesenchyme rather than Paneth cells as the ligand source. The lesson therefore presents this as a reading to hold open rather than as the established mechanism for the human colon.

claims.statement: In the modelled canonical Wnt pathway, doubling the Axin concentration causes a 50 per cent drop in the half-life of beta-catenin, while doubling GSK3B decreases that half-life by about 10 per cent.
claims.scope: The relative sensitivity of beta-catenin half-life to the concentrations of two destruction complex components, in a fitted model of the pathway.
claims.uncertainty: These are model sensitivities computed for a frog egg extract system, not measurements in a human crypt cell, and a doubling is a modelling perturbation rather than an experiment performed on tissue. The lesson uses them to compare two components within one model and does not claim the percentages transfer to any other system.

claims.statement: Axin is present at about 20 picomolar, much lower than the concentration of the other major components of the Wnt pathway, against an APC concentration of about 100 nanomolar.
claims.scope: The concentrations of Axin and APC reported in a quantitative study of the pathway, used to explain why the system's sensitivity is concentrated in Axin.
claims.uncertainty: Measured in Xenopus egg extracts, so the absolute concentrations are properties of that system. The lesson's explanation, that adding to the scarcest component changes throughput more than adding to an abundant one, is a reading of the scarcity together with the sensitivity result rather than a separate sourced finding.

claims.statement: About 93 per cent of colorectal cancers contain an activating mutation in the Wnt pathway, particularly in APC, and loss of APC function impairs the destruction complex and allows beta-catenin to accumulate.
claims.scope: The frequency of Wnt pathway activating mutations among colorectal cancers, and the molecular consequence of losing APC function, used to motivate why a positional-signal pathway matters clinically.
claims.uncertainty: A population-level frequency quoted in a review, not a personal risk and not a statement about any individual. It depends on the cohorts and sequencing methods behind it and on how an activating mutation is defined. The lesson makes no claim about how such a mutation leads to a tumour, about staging, screening, prognosis or treatment, and defers cancer mechanism to a later lesson in the block.

claims.statement: Components of the endogenous beta-catenin destruction complex gathered towards Wnt-coated beads in 61 to 80 per cent of human colon epithelial cells carrying full-length APC, fell to about 30 per cent in a line expressing truncated APC, and Wnt-induced localisation was abolished where APC had been deleted.
claims.scope: The dependence of Wnt-induced destruction complex relocalisation on full-length APC, measured by localisation frequency in cultured human colon epithelial cells.
claims.uncertainty: Localisation frequencies in cultured cells, several of them colorectal cancer lines, scored by immunofluorescence against beads presenting a localised Wnt cue. This is an experimental arrangement rather than a crypt, and the percentages should be read as the result of that assay.

claims.statement: Because APC is both a component of the destruction complex and required for the complex to relocate towards a Wnt cue, a cell with damaged APC accumulates beta-catenin and runs the beta-catenin-dependent gene programme whether or not Wnt has arrived, so its output no longer tracks the Wnt concentration around it and it behaves as a cell at the crypt base would behave, at any height.
claims.scope: An interpretation of two sourced molecular findings in terms of positional reading, offered to show what the lesson's model explains about the consequence of losing APC.
claims.uncertainty: This is the lesson's inference and is labelled as such in the scene. The sources establish that APC loss impairs the destruction complex and permits beta-catenin accumulation, and that full-length APC is needed for relocalisation towards a Wnt cue; neither states the positional conclusion in these terms. The strength of the decoupling will depend on which part of APC is lost and on what else the cell carries. The lesson makes no claim that this alone produces a tumour, and defers that question to a later lesson in the block.

claims.statement: The colon renews every three to five days, with enterocytes replaced every four to five days.
claims.scope: The renewal interval of the colonic epithelium, used to argue that the instruction to divide is issued and withdrawn continuously in this tissue.
claims.uncertainty: A population-level interval for healthy tissue; individual cell lifespans vary and some epithelial cell types in the same tissue persist far longer. The figures match those used by PREM-BIO-001, PREM-BIO-002, PREM-BIO-003 and PREM-BIO-004 and are kept identical for block continuity. The argument that rapid renewal makes loss of the withdrawal step more consequential here than in a slowly renewing tissue is the lesson's own reasoning.

claims.statement: This lesson borrows five things from protein chemistry: that a protein has a definite shape which binding can change; that one protein can have separable parts doing separable jobs, so a shortened protein can lose one function and keep others; that a scaffold protein holds other proteins together without doing the chemistry itself, APC and Axin acting as the scaffolds here; that a protein can be tagged with ubiquitin and destroyed in the proteasome; and that a conserved amino acid is one unchanged at that position across many species.
claims.scope: The minimum protein vocabulary this lesson uses, assembled so that the unwritten prerequisite lesson on protein structure and folding is named rather than silently assumed.
claims.uncertainty: Each item is stated at the level this lesson needs and no further. The scaffold role of APC and Axin comes from the 2003 quantitative study, the separability of one protein's functions from the 2020 truncated-APC result, the ubiquitin-proteasome route from the 2025 review, and the conserved serine from the 2021 review. How a sequence produces a fold, and how binding at one site changes another, are not explained here and belong to PREM-09.03, which has no lesson yet.

claims.statement: Beta-catenin exists in a cell in more than one pool: a large and highly stable share is bound to membrane E-cadherin and takes no part in canonical Wnt signalling, and the study measuring the pathway's dynamics removed that fraction before analysis. The quantity the pathway's measurements report is free non-phosphorylated beta-catenin, the pool neither held in the destruction complex nor yet phosphorylated.
claims.scope: The distinction between the E-cadherin-bound pool and the signalling pool of beta-catenin, used to fix what every concentration figure in this lesson refers to.
claims.uncertainty: The source reports the E-cadherin-associated pool for the cells it studied and describes it as reported rather than newly measured there. This lesson uses the distinction only to name its own quantity precisely, and quantifies no pool other than the free non-phosphorylated one.

claims.statement: How Wnt binding reduces beta-catenin destruction is not settled. Relocalisation of some destruction complexes to the membrane accounts for part of it, but residual phosphorylating activity after Wnt stimulation comes mainly from complexes that did not move and that remain intact and active in the cytoplasm. Two further mechanisms are proposed: temporary inactivation of the complex by saturation with already-phosphorylated beta-catenin, and release of a partner that prevents the ubiquitin-attaching enzyme from docking. The question is described in the literature as controversial.
claims.scope: The unsettled state of the step between Wnt binding and reduced beta-catenin destruction, and the specific mechanisms under consideration.
claims.uncertainty: This claim records that the question is open, which is what the source states; it is not a claim that any one mechanism is correct. The lesson notes that everything downstream in the pack depends only on the reduction in destruction rate, which every proposed mechanism delivers, so no teaching in this pack turns on which is right.

terms.definition: A molecule released by one cell whose presence and amount change what another cell does. The everyday sense of a signal, as in a traffic signal or a hand signal, keeps the part that matters: something is sent so that something else will change its behaviour. What biology adds is that the sender and receiver are cells and the message is a molecule, so the message carries no content beyond how much of it there is and where it binds. A signal does not name a state of affairs; the receiving cell's machinery supplies all of the interpretation. Distinct from a signal sequence, which is part of a protein's own chain and addresses the inside of one cell.

An extracellular signal molecule considered in its capacity as the thing that binds a receptor. Signal and ligand can pick out the same molecule; the word ligand puts the emphasis on the binding event rather than on the sending.

A protein that binds a particular signal and, as a consequence of binding it, changes what it does. A cell-surface receptor sits in the membrane with a part outside the cell and a part inside, so that a binding event on the outside becomes a change on the inside. In this lesson the Wnt receptor is a pair of proteins working together, Frizzled with LRP5/6, which is a reminder that one receptor function need not mean one receptor molecule.

The conversion of a binding event outside a cell into a change inside it. Cell-surface receptors act as signal transducers: they turn an extracellular ligand-binding event into intracellular signals that alter the target cell's behaviour. Transduction is a change of medium rather than a change of message, which is why the word is borrowed from engineering.

The return of a cell towards its unstimulated state when a signal is withdrawn. Termination is part of what makes a signal informative rather than a switch thrown once, and it is often supplied by the continual turnover of the molecules the signal alters. In the canonical Wnt pathway termination needs nothing new to be built, because the machinery that destroys the output is running at all times and simply resumes its usual effect.

A systematic difference in the amount of a substance across space, so that the concentration at one place differs from the concentration at another. In this lesson the gradient runs along the length of a crypt and the quantity that varies is a Wnt protein. The word describes the profile and not its cause: a falling profile can be produced by spreading and breakdown, or by handover between cells combined with dilution, and which of those builds the crypt gradient is unsettled. PREM-BIO-003's proton gradient is a difference of this kind across a membrane rather than along a tissue, and the two are separate cases of the same idea.

What a cell can determine about where it sits from a quantity it can measure locally. Treating it as information is what makes it countable: telling apart 32 positions demands five binary distinctions, and a single gene reading a single threshold on a gradient that falls in one direction supplies one, distinguishing two regions and no more. A gradient therefore supplies coarse zones rather than coordinates, and real systems exceed that ceiling by letting genes influence one another and by using graded expression rather than on-or-off calls.

A substance that spreads from a source and specifies what cells become according to its local concentration. Wnt in the colonic crypt fits the second half of that description comfortably: what a cell becomes does depend on how much reaches it. Whether it fits the first half in the classical sense of diffusive spreading is an open question, because Wnt proteins are lipid-modified and their mode of travel is debated. This lesson uses the word for the role Wnt plays and not as a claim about how it moves.

A family of secreted signalling proteins, and in this lesson the signal that reports height in the colonic crypt. Mesenchymal cells near the crypt base secrete them and cells further away do not, so Wnt activity falls progressively up the crypt axis. Wnt proteins carry a lipid modification that makes them hydrophobic, which is required for their secretion and is also what makes their travel through watery extracellular space difficult to explain.

The assembly that keeps free beta-catenin scarce in a cell receiving no Wnt. It includes APC, Axin and the kinases CK1A and GSK3B; beta-catenin is drawn in, phosphorylated, then tagged with ubiquitin and destroyed in the proteasome. Wnt binding reduces the rate of that destruction, so the pathway raises its output by interfering with destruction instead of increasing production. How the reduction happens is not settled: some complexes relocate to the membrane while remaining assembled, but the complexes that stay in the cytosol remain active, and saturation of the complex or blocking of the ubiquitin-tagging step are both proposed to account for the rest.

The protein whose amount carries the Wnt signal inside the cell. It exists in more than one pool, and only one of them matters here: a large, highly stable share is bound to E-cadherin at the membrane and takes no part in canonical Wnt signalling. **Free beta-catenin**, the quantity every figure in this lesson refers to, is the pool neither held inside the destruction complex nor yet phosphorylated; sources also call it free non-phosphorylated beta-catenin, or available beta-catenin. It is made continuously and, without Wnt, destroyed continuously, so its level reports the balance of synthesis against destruction. Free beta-catenin that escapes destruction enters the nucleus and acts with TCF and LEF.

A large scaffolding protein of the beta-catenin destruction complex, present at about 100 nanomolar in the system where the pathway was quantified. It has two roles in this lesson: it belongs to the complex that marks beta-catenin for destruction, and full-length APC is required for that complex to reorient towards a localised Wnt cue. Damage to it therefore leaves beta-catenin accumulating whether or not Wnt has arrived. The gene encoding it carries the same name.

A protein that binds to DNA or to a DNA-bound partner and changes whether nearby genes are transcribed. TCF and LEF are the transcription factors that beta-catenin partners in this pathway, which is how a concentration outside the cell becomes a change in which genes are read.

A relay chain that contains multiple amplification steps. The definition matters because the word is often applied to any multi-step pathway and the amplification then read back out of the label. Whether a given chain earns the word is a question to answer with evidence about its steps: phototransduction has two identifiable multiplying steps, while the canonical Wnt pathway's identifiable catalytic steps sit on the arm that destroys its output.

A step at which one activated molecule causes many molecules to be activated, converted or modified, so the number affected grows along the chain. Amplification is a property of individual steps rather than of pathways as a whole, and a pathway can contain a strongly amplifying step while showing a small change in output, when that step sits on the arm removing the response. Gains are also reported in more than one kind of unit: a per-event catalytic tally (molecules consumed per input event) is a different quantity from a ratio of two steady-state levels, and the two cannot be divided into one another. In the canonical Wnt pathway the catalytic steps belong to the kinases that mark beta-catenin for destruction.

A cell with the capacity to self-renew and to produce differentiated progeny. The definition is about capacity rather than continuous activity: some stem-cell populations are quiescent until activated, while others cycle actively. In this lesson the term names the cells at the crypt base, which are the cells with the highest Wnt activity and whose gene programme this lesson's pathway switches on.

alignment.note: PREM-BIO-001 defines stem cell for this course and this lesson keeps that meaning without alteration: capacity to self-renew and to produce differentiated progeny, with capacity distinguished from continuous division. Nothing is narrowed or extended here. What this lesson adds is the mechanism by which the crypt-base population's programme is switched on, which PREM-BIO-001 deferred to a later lesson in the block.

Lesson content licence

The teaching content of this pack, including all scene prose, the declarative diagram, the assessment items and answer keys, the glossary and the claim ledger, is original to this pack and is released under CC BY 4.0. Facts drawn from the sources listed in references.json are used as facts. No source's wording, figure, table, schematic, dataset, question or example is reproduced or adapted anywhere in this pack.

Assets

Original assets. One, declared in lesson.json under originalAssets:

  • diagrams/wnt-reception-to-response.diagram.json — a declarative flow diagram of canonical Wnt signalling in a colonic crypt cell, seven stages and six links, written for this lesson. Its longDescription is a faithful text equivalent of the same graph and states every node, every edge, the direction of each edge, which two edges are inhibitory, and the conclusion the shape of the graph supports.

Third-party assets. None. The thirdPartyAssets array in lesson.json is empty, and no scene uses a {figure} directive.

The block brief records that this outcome has no correctly-licensed third-party figure available, so the signalling figure is original by design rather than by omission. A search for a reusable figure was not conducted against smart.servier.com, whose entry in site/agent/source-access-ledger.json is human-only: its terms of use forbid automated access even though the medical images themselves carry CC BY 4.0. An authoring agent may not fetch from that host, and the ledger's note that the same art is mirrored on Wikimedia Commons under a superseded share-alike licence rules that route out as well.

Sources

Twelve sources are recorded in references.json and every one was retrieved and read directly by this run. Every asserted fact in the scenes maps to a claim in claims.json, and every claim appears in a learner-visible {source-note} in each scene where it is used.

Sources by host:

  • pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov (ten sources). Recorded allowed in the source-access ledger, whose entry cites robots.txt carrying Allow: /articles/. Nguyen, Lausten & Boman 2025 on the colonic crypt; Parker & Neufeld 2020 on APC and destruction complex recruitment in human colonocytes; Lee, Salic, Krüger, Heinrich & Kirschner 2003 on the quantitative Wnt pathway; Goentoro & Kirschner 2009 on fold-change readout; Mehta, Hingole & Chaudhary 2021 on Wnt secretion mechanisms; Hillenbrand, Gerland & Tkačik 2016 on positional information beyond the French flag model; Tostevin, ten Wolde & Howard 2007 on the fundamental limits to position determination; van der Wath, Gardiner, Burgess & Smith 2013 on crypt geometry; Baker and colleagues 2014 on crypt migration speed; Mukherjee, Dhar, Stathos, Schaffer & Kane 2018 on how Wnt influences destruction complex activity.
  • www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov (two sources, both NCBI Bookshelf chapters of Molecular Biology of the Cell, 4th edition). This host is recorded restricted in the ledger because robots.txt disallows the legacy /pmc/articles route for unnamed agents. That restriction does not reach the Bookshelf chapter route. This run retrieved and read the full robots.txt before access and confirmed that the wildcard User-agent: * block disallows /pmc/articles and a set of query and tool paths, that its only books rule is Disallow: /books/?term=, which covers the search query route and not chapter pages, and that the file names no AI or LLM crawler and carries no rule applying to this agent. A Crawl-delay: 5 applies and was respected. The same route and the same finding are recorded by the earlier published pack PREM-BIO-004.

No new domain was checked, so site/agent/source-access-ledger.json was deliberately left unmodified. Both hosts used already have entries within the ledger's 90-day recheck window. The additional detail this run established about the Bookshelf route is recorded in the agentAccess notes of the two affected source records instead of in the shared ledger, because a second agent was authoring in the same worktree concurrently and an unnecessary write to a shared file risks clobbering its append.

No source was retrieved from a domain marked excluded or human-only. No login, paywall or access control was bypassed anywhere in this run.

Known limitations of this pack

These are recorded deliberately. An honest gap is more useful to a reviewer than a confident guess.

1. The protein prerequisite has no lesson. This outcome declares two graph prerequisites, and one of them, topic-biomolecules-proteins (PREM-09.03, "Protein structure and folding"), has no published lesson anywhere in the corpus. That gap bites directly on this material, because a receptor is a protein and what a receptor does on binding a ligand is change shape. This pack does not re-teach protein structure and folding and does not paper over the absence. Scene 1 names the dependency explicitly, says that PREM-09.03 will own it, says it should be read first once it exists, and reduces what this lesson needs to a single stated sentence: a protein has a definite shape, and binding something can change it. Nothing downstream in the pack requires more protein chemistry than that. What a learner will therefore not get here is any account of how a sequence produces a fold, why a binding site has a particular geometry, or how binding at one end of a protein moves the other end.

2. No receptor copy number. The noise argument in scene 3 depends on a cell counting randomly arriving molecules at a finite number of receptors. No published figure for the number of Wnt receptors on a human colonic crypt cell was found, and none is supplied. Scene 3 says so in a scoping callout rather than substituting a plausible number.

3. The noise limit is transferred from a subcellular model. source-tostevin-position-limits models gradients used for positioning inside a single cell, of the kind bacteria use to find their own middle, not a tissue-scale gradient across an epithelium. The pack transfers only the structure of the argument and the square-root scaling of precision with averaging time, both consequences of molecules arriving at random, and states the limitation where it is used.

4. The positional information figure is from an insect. The 4.2-bit estimate is for the Drosophila gap genes, in a syncytium of nuclei sharing a cytoplasm. No equivalent measurement for the human colonic crypt was found. The scene states this and does not present the figure as the crypt's value.

5. The Wnt gain figure is a model of a frog extract. The approximately sixfold rise in free non-phosphorylated beta-catenin comes from a fitted model supported by measurements in Xenopus egg extracts, not from a measurement inside a human crypt cell, and the comparison with phototransduction sets a modelled figure beside textbook figures from a different system. Both scenes that use it say so. The comparison is offered to show that measured gains differ by orders of magnitude, not to rank the two pathways precisely.

6. Gradient formation is unsettled and is left unsettled. How a Wnt gradient forms is genuinely open, and scene 5 presents the competing readings with the observation behind each rather than choosing one. The short-range lateral transcytosis result is reported in a 2021 review of a 2016 primary study; the primary study was not itself retrieved, and the pack attributes the finding to work reported in the review rather than presenting it first-hand. That work is in mouse small intestine and concerns Wnt3, whereas this block follows the human colonic crypt, where the same review identifies the mesenchyme as the ligand source.

7. The destruction complex composition is stated non-exhaustively on purpose. source-nguyen-colonic-crypt lists Dishevelled among the complex's components. Dishevelled's placement is described differently across the literature, so this pack names only APC, Axin, CK1A and GSK3B, says the complex "includes" them, and records the divergence in scene 2's source note and in the claim's uncertainty field. Nothing taught here depends on settling it.

8. The positional interpretation of APC loss is an inference. That a cell with damaged APC reports the crypt base at any height is this pack's reading of two sourced molecular findings, not a quoted conclusion. claim-apc-loss-decouples-readout records it as support: inference at medium confidence, and the scene labels it as an interpretation.

9. Amplification is the one job of five not traced through Wnt itself. The outcome asks for reception, transduction, amplification, response and termination. Four of those are traced through the crypt's own Wnt pathway. Amplification is traced through vertebrate phototransduction, whose per-step figures are published, and through a composite pathway written for scene 6's audit. The reason is stated in scene 4 rather than hidden: no source consulted here reports a per-event catalytic gain for any step of the canonical Wnt pathway, and the transcriptional step in particular is left unaudited because no figure was found that this pack could stand behind. What the pack does establish about Wnt is where its multiplying steps sit, namely on the arm that destroys the output, and what its output ratio is. What it cannot state is by how much any single Wnt step multiplies.

10. The two gain figures are not commensurable, and the pack says so instead of comparing them. An earlier draft divided phototransduction's tally of more than 100,000 molecules per absorbed photon by the Wnt pathway's roughly sixfold change and reported a four-orders-of-magnitude difference. That comparison is invalid: the first is a per-event catalytic count with units, the second a dimensionless ratio of two steady-state concentrations. Scene 4 now names the error explicitly, an assessment item uses the invalid division as its most attractive distractor, and no numerical comparison between the two pathways' gains is asserted anywhere in the pack.

11. How Wnt slows destruction is unsettled, and the pack carries all the candidates. Scene 2 originally joined "the complex is recruited to the membrane" and "available beta-catenin rises" with an "and", leaving the causal step blank. It now reports what the sources support: relocation of some complexes is real and is the authors' proposal, relocation alone does not account for the loss of activity because the complexes that stay in the cytosol remain active, and saturation of the complex or interruption of the ubiquitin-tagging step are both proposed for the remainder. The literature calls the question controversial and the pack does not resolve it. Nothing taught in the pack depends on which mechanism wins, because every candidate delivers the same reduction in destruction rate.

Deliberate scope exclusions

  • Non-canonical Wnt signalling. The planar cell polarity and calcium branches are not covered. The outcome is served by tracing one pathway completely rather than surveying several partially.
  • A survey of receptor classes and second messengers. G-protein-linked receptors appear only as the contrasting high-gain case in scene 4. Ion channels, enzyme-linked receptors and intracellular receptors are not covered.
  • Cancer mechanism. Scene 7 sets up topic-cell-biology-cell-death-cancer (PREM-05.10) and stops. How a decoupled readout becomes a tumour, what else must go wrong, and anything about staging, screening, prognosis or treatment are outside this pack.
  • Gradient shape from first principles. No calculation of a concentration profile from a diffusion coefficient is attempted, because scene 5 establishes that the mechanism of spread is the disputed part.
  • Membrane structure and fluidity. Owned by PREM-BIO-004 and adopted rather than re-taught.
